On the map, Iroquois marks the lands of the Haudenosaunee Confederacy from 1500 to 1715, in what is now upstate New York. The five nations, Mohawk, Oneida, Onondaga, Cayuga and Seneca, were bound by the Great Law of Peace and met in council at Onondaga.

These were the years of their greatest power. Dutch traders at New Netherland sold them muskets for beaver pelts. In the Beaver Wars of the 1600s the Haudenosaunee fought for control of the fur trade and broke up neighbouring peoples:

  • the Wendat (Huron) in 1649
  • the Neutral and the Erie in the 1650s

Captives were adopted to replace the dead. The wars with New France ended in the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701, after which the confederacy balanced between the French and the English. Around 1722 the Tuscarora came north from Carolina and joined as the sixth nation.
